title: New Construction Exemption
text: The Haryana Urban (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1973 does not apply to a building for ten years from the date its construction is completed, an exemption intended to encourage new construction, and the Act also does not extend to cantonment areas. A lease for a recently constructed property in Haryana may therefore fall outside the Act's rent and eviction protections during this window.
source: Haryana Urban (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1973, Section 1(3) (as amended by Haryana Act 16 of 1978)

title: Cap on Advance Rent; No Premium Allowed
text: Under the Haryana Urban (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1973, a landlord may not charge any premium, salami, or other lump sum in addition to rent, and may only demand advance rent of up to one month's rent. A lease clause demanding a larger upfront deposit or premium beyond one month's rent is inconsistent with the Act.
source: Haryana Urban (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1973, Section 6

title: Fair Rent Determination and Increase Cap
text: The Rent Controller may fix 'fair rent' for a building on application by either party, allowing an increase or decrease of up to 25% tied to movement in the All India Wholesale Price Index since the base agreement date; once fair rent is fixed, no further increase is permitted for five years except where the landlord has funded improvements at the tenant's request. This limits how much a landlord can lawfully raise rent on premises covered by the Act.
source: Haryana Urban (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1973, Sections 4 and 5(1)

title: Restricted Grounds for Eviction
text: A landlord may evict a tenant under the Haryana Urban (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1973 only on specified grounds, including non-payment of rent within 15 days of the due date, subletting or transfer without written consent, misuse causing material damage to the building, nuisance to neighbours, continuous non-occupation for four months or more, or the landlord's bona fide personal or government-service need for the premises. Eviction outside these grounds is not permitted for premises the Act covers.
source: Haryana Urban (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1973, Section 13

title: Landlord Repair and Amenity Obligations
text: Landlords must carry out necessary (non-structural) repairs to the premises and must provide basic amenities such as water supply, electricity, and sewerage connections where available in the locality; if a landlord neglects repairs after notice, the tenant may apply to the Rent Controller to have the work done and deduct the cost from rent. A lease clause pushing all repair responsibility onto the tenant may conflict with this obligation.
source: Haryana Urban (Control of Rent and Eviction) Act, 1973, Sections 9 and 12
